_note: Episode 8 version 2 (the new form, as Episode 1 v2). Every still is one full painted picture in the Bakunawa look (the JSON prompt of pipeline/draw_pick.py, three draws a key, the choice at 3x). 'full' holds each still's JSON prompt; bk_NN = row NN of shots.md; bk_02b is the second close-up of shot 2 (her eyes). 'shots' maps every sentence 0-76 to the still it shows; keys 90-96 are the silent shots, shown inside one sentence each through shots_fx 'keys': shot 9 (hammock) key 90 in sentence 21, shot 13 (lens raised) key 91 in 28, shot 15 (the woman in the salakot) key 92 in 34, shot 20 (the toddler's eyes) key 93 in 45, shot 22 (the wrist let go) key 94 in 51, shot 30 (the umbrella drawn) key 95 in 67, shot 33 (the dot in the west) key 96 in 72. Shot 37 (trivia card) is not drawn. Rules kept: Kawit only from the BACK of the crowd (backs, hats, trays, the hammock, the lens); never the window, the flag, a drum, open hands pushing toward us or a crowd parting from the front; the earlier Indio only tiny inside the lens circle (bk_14). Mabini is a generic thin man, no likeness, carried in a hammock, lying or half-seated, never standing, never comic. M wears period clothes and a salakot (as Episode 3) and her face IS seen (bk_02b, bk_19); she wears no coat and no medallion of her own here, so only the family medallion is in the picture. The red umbrella appears only folded and only from bk_30. Indio has no medallion (M took it in Episode 6): five indigo lines until bk_26, six from bk_27 on. The voice of Sulayman is light only (bk_24): no figure, no face. The lens (lente) string is from story/ep07_v2/shots.md ('an old lens with a gold rim'; through it 'tinted warm and slightly curved'), because videos/ep07v2-ang-sulat-ni-lolo/key_prompts.json has no prompts yet: when Episode 7 v2 draws its lens, copy its exact words into look_cast.cast.lente and lens_view here before drawing. Writing in pictures, added in code after the choice: bk_36 the episode's question ("Ikaw, ka-Indio: kung isang hakbang na lang pauwi, at may nagsabing \"huwag muna\", makikinig ka ba?") in the bare upper wall, about 8% to 40% of the height, clear of the subtitle band at 63%. Nothing else is written: the tally marks of bk_04 and bk_36 are marks drawn by the model (groups of five, no numerals; the count is not meant to be read), the map of bk_32 and bk_33 is coastlines and dots with no labels, the phone screen of bk_35 is a plain glow, the sheet of bk_31 is blank. Negative for every draw: flat cel shading, flat even lighting, cartoon, tv animation, thick even outlines, poster, clip art, text, letters, numbers, watermark, extra fingers, flag, window, drum, balcony, modern buildings, electric wires, weapons, blades.

bk_20.setting: a dusty yard in Kawit, Cavite, on the afternoon of 12 June 1898, the crowd soft and out of focus behind; no flag, no modern buildings
bk_20.light: soft golden afternoon light on the child's face, gentle shadows, quiet, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
bk_20.note: silent shot 20 (key 93, inside sentence 45); the eyes are the shot

bk_21.subject: Close-up, long hold: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, a red cloth headband with long tails, wearing a loose white collarless camisa shirt with the sleeves rolled above the elbows, a plain flour-dusted cotton apron, rolled-up dark trousers, barefoot, bare neck with no necklace and no medallion, exactly five thin straight indigo line tattoos across his right forearm, the anger draining out of his face, his jaw loosening, eyes wet, looking sideways straight at the viewer. His face in the upper half of the picture. Hands below the frame. No other people.
bk_21.setting: a dusty yard in Kawit, Cavite, on the afternoon of 12 June 1898, the crowd soft and out of focus behind; no flag, no modern buildings
bk_21.light: warm late golden sun turning soft, long shadows, dust slowly falling, rim light, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
bk_21.note: his look to us; hands hidden

bk_22.subject: Close-up on hands: a woman's fingers in a thin dark cloth glove opening and letting go of a young man's floury wrist; his free right hand, a thumb and four fingers, hanging in the air, then drawing slowly back; five thin straight indigo line tattoos on the forearm. Only the two hands and forearms, no faces. The hands in the upper half.
bk_22.setting: a dusty yard in Kawit, Cavite, on the afternoon of 12 June 1898, the crowd soft and out of focus behind; no flag, no modern buildings
bk_22.light: soft golden afternoon light, flour dust drifting down, gentle shadows, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
bk_22.note: silent shot 22 (key 94, sentence 51); hands are the shot: count fingers; a wrist released, NOT a hand held

bk_23.subject: Medium shot: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, a red cloth headband with long tails, wearing a loose white collarless camisa shirt with the sleeves rolled above the elbows, a plain flour-dusted cotton apron, rolled-up dark trousers, barefoot, bare neck with no necklace and no medallion, exactly five thin straight indigo line tattoos across his right forearm, nodding once, slowly, his chin down, mouth firm, a quiet decision on his face. His face in the upper half. Arms at his sides, hands below the frame. Behind him, out of focus, backs of the crowd.
bk_23.setting: a dusty yard in Kawit, Cavite, on the afternoon of 12 June 1898, the crowd soft and out of focus behind; no flag, no modern buildings
bk_23.light: low amber late-afternoon sun, long blue shadows, dust and flour motes in the air, warm rim light, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork

bk_24.subject: Close-up: two gloved hands lowering the worn cord of an old round bronze medallion engraved with a sun and a triangle, on a worn cord over the small head of a Filipino toddler about two years old, round cheeks, short soft black hair, a small plain white cotton shirt, calm deep dark eyes that look old and kind; where the bronze touches the child's chest a faint ring of soft golden light. The medallion and the child's face in the upper half. The woman's face out of the picture.
bk_24.setting: a dusty yard in Kawit, Cavite, on the afternoon of 12 June 1898, the crowd soft and out of focus behind; no flag, no modern buildings

bk_25.subject: Two-shot: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, a red cloth headband with long tails, wearing a loose white collarless camisa shirt with the sleeves rolled above the elbows, a plain flour-dusted cotton apron, rolled-up dark trousers, barefoot, bare neck with no necklace and no medallion, exactly five thin straight indigo line tattoos across his right forearm, startled, turning his head this way and that, looking for a voice; beside him a calm young Filipina woman in her twenties with long straight black hair tied low at the nape, a tired gentle face, dark eyes, a wide woven salakot hat, wearing a plain faded indigo baro blouse, a long dark patadyong skirt and a dark brown cotton shawl over her shoulders, thin dark cloth gloves, with a small knowing smile. Both faces in the upper half. Hands below the frame.

bk_26.subject: Close-up of a young man's right forearm, white with flour: five thin straight indigo line tattoos, and a sixth new line burning through the flour beside them, glowing hot gold, a thin curl of smoke rising; the rolled white sleeve at the top; the hand relaxed, out of the picture. The forearm in the upper half.

bk_28.subject: Low-angle comic shot: a strong Filipina baker woman of about fifty, broad shoulders, thick forearms dusted with flour, greying black hair under a faded red kerchief tied over her head, a weathered round face, a plain brown baro blouse with rolled sleeves, a long dark skirt, a flour-stained apron, standing on an upturned wooden crate, mouth wide bawling at the crowd, a bread roll held in each fist, one roll pointing toward the side of the picture. Her face and fists in the upper half of the picture. Hats of the crowd at the bottom edge.
bk_28.setting: the side edge of a crowd in a dusty yard in Kawit, Cavite, on the afternoon of 12 June 1898: a bamboo fence, coconut palms, nipa huts, backs and straw hats; no flag, no modern buildings, no electric wires
bk_28.light: low amber late-afternoon sun, long blue shadows, dust and flour motes in the air, warm rim light, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
bk_28.note: comic; fists closed around the rolls

bk_29.subject: Wide shot from behind him: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, a red cloth headband with long tails, wearing a loose white collarless camisa shirt with the sleeves rolled above the elbows, a plain flour-dusted cotton apron, rolled-up dark trousers, barefoot, bare neck with no necklace and no medallion, exactly six thin straight indigo line tattoos across his right forearm, seen from behind, his ears bright red; the people at the back of the crowd turning round toward him, grinning, raising bread rolls to him like toasts; beside his leg a medium-sized slim black short-haired Philippine street dog with a white chest patch, one folded ear and bright clever eyes, a red kerchief around his neck. The dog's left ear stands upright and pointed, only the dog's right ear is folded down; the dog's face is all black with no white on it, the white patch is only on the dog's chest. Grinning. The turning faces in the upper half.
bk_29.setting: a dusty yard in Kawit, Cavite, on the afternoon of 12 June 1898: bamboo fences, coconut palms, backs and hats of a crowd; no flag, no modern buildings, no electric wires
bk_29.light: low amber late-afternoon sun, long blue shadows, dust and flour motes in the air, warm rim light, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
bk_29.note: from behind Indio; the back rows turn round; not a parted crowd

bk_30.subject: Close-up on hands: two hands in thin dark cloth gloves drawing a folded red umbrella with a thick carved dark wooden handle, closed and tied from under a dark brown cotton shawl and twisting its handle; the top of the handle swings open like a little box lid. Only the hands, the shawl and the umbrella, no faces. The handle in the upper half.

bk_30.light: warm low sun, the red cloth glowing, deep shadows in the shawl, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork

bk_31.subject: Macro shot into the hollow of an opened carved wooden umbrella handle: inside it a small star-shaped bronze medallion the size of a coin, with five points and a small rolled sheet of old yellowed paper, completely blank, tied with a thread. The star and the paper in the upper half of the picture; the red cloth of the umbrella at the edge. No hands.

bk_31.light: a single warm ray of sun into the hollow, the bronze star gleaming, soft sparkles, deep shadow around, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork

bk_32.subject: View seen through the gold-rimmed circle of the lens: everything inside the circle tinted warm and slightly curved, outside the circle dark and blurred: held over a flat sheet of old yellowed paper; inside the circle faint brown ink lines of coastlines appearing on the paper and twelve small glowing gold dots spread across it; outside the circle the paper stays blank. The circle in the upper half. No hands.

The circle and the glowing dot in the upper half. No hands.

bk_34.subject: Medium shot in profile: a young Filipino man about twenty, lean, warm brown skin, short tousled black hair tied in a small topknot, dark brown eyes, a red cloth headband with long tails, wearing a loose white collarless camisa shirt with the sleeves rolled above the elbows, a plain flour-dusted cotton apron, rolled-up dark trousers, barefoot, bare neck with no necklace and no medallion, exactly six thin straight indigo line tattoos across his right forearm, looking off into the far distance toward home, then back down, shaking his head with half a smile, steady and at peace. His face in the upper half of the picture. Hands below the frame.

bk_35.subject: Long-lens shot, rack focus: in the foreground two woven straw hats of men in the crowd, seen from behind, soft and out of focus at the sides; between them, sharp, a raised arm in the sleeve of a modern dark blue zip-up sports jacket, holding up a glowing smartphone with a small round ring light clipped to its top, the screen a plain white glow, held high above the hats, the man's face hidden behind the hats. The phone in the upper half, the brightest thing in the picture.
bk_35.setting: the back of a huge crowd in a dusty yard and road in Kawit, Cavite, on the afternoon of 12 June 1898: bamboo fences, nipa huts, coconut palms, a big old wooden house far off, hidden by heads and hats; no flag, no modern buildings, no electric wires
bk_35.light: low amber late-afternoon sun, the phone and ring light glowing cold white against the warm dusty air, long shadows, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
bk_35.note: must read at a glance: modern sleeve, phone, ring light; face hidden

bk_36.subject: Front view, flat and still: a rough lime-washed bakery wall, its upper part bare and plain, rows of short black charcoal tally marks across the middle of the wall only, an empty round bilao tray leaning below. No people, no dog.
bk_36.setting: inside a small old bakery of 1898 in Cavite: a rough lime-washed wall covered with rows and rows of short black charcoal tally marks, each group four upright strokes crossed by a fifth, beside a domed brick oven; no letters, no numbers, no modern things
bk_36.light: quiet evening, the oven coals dimmed to a low red glow, soft warm shadows, richly painted, detailed ink linework, textured brushwork
bk_36.note: the question is added in code in the bare upper part (about 8% to 40% of the height)
